conclusion.text: Question Does DECT provide superior diagnostic accuracy compared to conventional CT in detecting appendicular fractures across different anatomical sites? items.title: The Prognostic Value of PSMA-total Tumor Volume for Overall Survival in mHSPC: Exploratory Evaluation Within the ENZAMET Trial and PROMISE Registry.
items.authors: Karpinski MJ, Sabahi Z, Herrmann K, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml from an ENZAMET cohort is prognostic for OS in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort. Further validation of PSMA-TTV as a prognostic biomarker with potential to be a predictive marker to identify patients for intensification is warranted.

extras.label: Results and limitations
extras.text: Overall, 100 patients from ENZAMET and 993 patients from the PROMISE Registry were analyzed. The upper ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV category was ≥72 ml. In patients with CHAARTED criteria low-volume disease, 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml versus <72 ml was 36% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 16-83) versus 71% (60-85; p = 0.019) in survival curves; 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml was not associated with shorter OS in the ENZAMET subgroup (50% [32-78] vs 73% [63-85]; p = 0.063) but in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup (33% [27-40] vs 78% [75-81]; p < 0.001). The hazard ratio for upper PSMA-TTV category ≥72 ml was 6.8 (95% CI = 5.3-8.7) in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup.

extras.label: Key points

items.title: Radiogenomic profile of PIK3CA mutation in lung cancer: PET/CT findings, co-mutation patterns, and exploratory survival associations.
items.authors: Göksel S, Boyacıoğlu SÖ, Öztürk H, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: PIK3CA-mutated NSCLC tumors showed higher metabolic activity, particularly higher SUVmax values, than PIK3CA-wild-type tumors. However, SUVmax demonstrated only modest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.703), with substantial overlap between mutation groups. These findings support an association between PIK3CA mutation status and tumor glucose metabolism rather than a clinically applicable imaging-based prediction model. FDG PET/CT cannot substitute for molecular testing, and the present study does not establish a role for PET/CT parameters in treatment selection. Further prospective and externally validated studies incorporating standardized treatment, staging, and follow-up data are required to determine the clinical relevance of these radiogenomic and survival associations.

fig.cap: A 78-year-old male patient with a history of bilateral renal lesions (left, 7 × 2.9 cm; right, 3 × 2.5 cm) and a suspected osseous lesion of the left fourth rib. PET/CT scan with low-dose CT acquired on day 5 after intravenous administration of 37 MBq [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab and was performed following left nephrectomy. The scan demonstrated marked CAIX-avid tracer uptake in the right renal lesion and multiple osseous lesions, including the left fourth and sixth ribs and the medial border of the right scapula (blue arrows on corresponding localized images). Two additional CAIX-avid thyroid lesions were identified - collectively indicated by red arrows on the whole-body PET image. Histopathological examination of the rib lesion confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The thyroid lesions were not biopsied and therefore remained of undetermined origin. PET/CT did not result in a direct change in management but confirmed CAIX-avid metastatic osseous disease

items.authors: Bhatia HS, Razavi AC, Dardari Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The CAC volume and density score, which adjusts CAC volume downward for higher density, and can be calculated from existing CAC reports, significantly improves risk discrimination and reclassification compared with the Agatston score.

items.title: Improved Visualization of Heart Valves With 4D-CT Using a Novel Motion Correction Algorithm.
items.authors: Zedler D, Demmert TT, Ritter A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: A novel motion correction algorithm substantially reduced motion artifacts and improved image quality in both native and prosthetic heart valve imaging with PCD-CT, with the largest improvements in systole. These benefits resulted in enhanced visualization of valvular pathology, potentially reinforcing the growing clinical role of cardiac CT for the assessment of valve disease.

items.title: 177Lu-Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen Prior to Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy in Oligorecurrent Prostate Cancer: Secondary and Exploratory End Point Results from the Randomized Phase 2 LUNAR Trial.
items.authors: Kishan AU, Wilhalme H, Felix C, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant 177Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

items.title: Associations between tissue stiffness, tumor response to transarterial chemoembolization and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma: insights from multifrequency 3D-magnetic resonance elastography.
items.authors: Chen J, Zhang Z, Ye Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

items.title: Subclinical leaflet thrombosis, transcatheter heart valve characteristics and structural valve deterioration: Rationale and design of the POPular PET TAVI study.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
items.authors: van Ginkel DJ, Overduin DC, Craig NJ, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The POPular PET TAVI study evaluates the interplay between subclinical leaflet thrombosis, THV characteristics, and structural valve deterioration at five years after TAVI. Improved understanding of these mechanisms may inform individualized antithrombotic strategies and optimized valve design, aiming to enhance long-term valve durability.

items.title: Guideline-endorsed but devalued: Fee schedule-wide and code-specific declines in Medicare payment for cardiac computed tomography, 2010-2026.
items.authors: Naeem M, French RJ, Rojas CA, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Medicare payment for cardiac CT has declined steeply in real terms since Category I code adoption, and the decline accelerated during the period of strongest guideline endorsement. It exceeded the decline of a non-cardiac comparator and was insensitive to the choice of deflator. This discordance has implications for access, service-line viability, and payment policy advocacy. Aggregate fee schedule spending nonetheless rose over 2013-2024, driven entirely by volume growth rather than by valuation.

items.title: Absolute myocardial blood flow via single-time-point imaging in positron emission tomography and single-photon emission computed tomography: Cross-validation against dynamic 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography.
items.journal_full: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
items.authors: Namías M, San Pedro AP, Pelegrina LT, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The simplified STP approach provides reliable MBF and MFR estimates from standard static scans, showing strong agreement with dynamic 13N-ammonia PET. By eliminating the requirement for full dynamic protocols, this method facilitates absolute flow quantification using existing conventional SPECT infrastructure.

items.title: CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.authors: Tan Y, Xu S, Liu X, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: CT radiomics and topology-based ITH features showed external predictive value for nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. The stacking model had the highest external AUC, but its improvement over radiomics alone was not statistically significant. If prospectively validated, these CT-based approaches could complement tissue assessment for pretreatment biological stratification.

items.title: Development and validation of a preoperative CT-based radiomics nomogram for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis after pancreatoduodenectomy.
items.authors: Chen H, Sun L, Liu J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The radiomics-integrated model demonstrated promising performance for preoperative prediction of PPAP after PD, which may facilitate individualized risk stratification and perioperative management.

items.title: MRI-derived radiomics for prostate cancer active surveillance: a systematic review.
items.authors: Kyle ET, Sweeney KJ, McCabe DH, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Progression endpoints were heterogeneous and several were of limited clinical relevance. A core outcome set for AS (at least ISUP grade group ≥3 and/or unequivocal radiological progression), followed by multi-centre external validation with a head-to-head comparison against the PRECISE v2 (Prostate Cancer Radiological Estimation of Change in Sequential Evaluation) score, is the priority before clinical use can be considered.

items.title: Multiparametric MRI assessment of renal Masses: Diagnostic performance of the modified clear cell likelihood score and ancillary MRI features.
items.authors: Asfuroğlu U, Cindil E, Kalafat B, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Incorporation of pseudocapsule assessment into the ccLS improved differentiation between benign and malignant renal masses while maintaining comparable diagnostic performance for identifying ccRCC. T2 SI ratio may provide additional value in MRI-based characterization of renal masses.

items.title: Utility of PSA density velocity in diagnosing prostate cancer on prostate MR.
items.authors: Narayanasamy S, Kurata Y, Kido A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Higher PSAD-velocity was associated with presence of csPCa on univariate analysis but not on multivariate analysis, and on fixed-model analysis did not meaningfully improve diagnostic discrimination beyond established predictors.

items.title: Abdominal hydatid disease and its mimics: a comprehensive pictorial review of imaging clues to the differential diagnosis.
items.authors: Shabana A, Elkasabi AY, Neimatallah M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Recognizing the characteristic imaging features of HD and its mimics is essential for accurate diagnosis and appropriate management. A systematic approach that incorporates lesion morphology, organ involvement, disease stage, and relevant clinical and epidemiological information can improve diagnostic confidence, enable early diagnosis, and help avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate intervention.

items.title: The diagnostic value of high-resolution 3D T2-weighted MRI in preoperative evaluation and classification of Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome: a prospective study.
items.authors: Qi Y, Song S, Gao X, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: High-resolution 3D T2 MRI is superior to conventional T2 TSE sequences in the preoperative evaluation of HWWS, especially for identifying communications and precisely locating obstruction sites.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Accurate preoperative structural assessment and classification of HWWS are clinically essential, yet conventional MRI has limitations in identifying fine anatomical structures and small communications. Findings High-resolution 3D T2 MRI outperforms conventional T2 TSE in identifying vaginal and cervical communications and precisely localizing obstruction sites in preoperative evaluation of HWWS.

conclusion.text: As the patient was oligometastatic, refractory to previous systemic therapies, and ineligible for surgery or radiotherapy, 177Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy was initiated.
